concept: Terraform management of asymmetric sharded clusters (replication_specs, use_effective_fields)

claims.text: Terraform considers ignored attributes during resource creation but ignores them when planning updates; map and list elements can be addressed by index. Ignoring a spec field can therefore also suppress a deliberate HCL size change. HashiCorp documents these semantics, and Scalr’s operational guidance warns to remove an attribute from ignore_changes before intentionally changing it. (high confidence)

The current advanced_cluster resource documentation states that use_effective_fields = true has no effect for clusters with more than one replication_specs entry and recommends leaving it disabled for those clusters. This explicit limitation scopes the sharding guide’s broader recommendation to enable the flag for per-shard auto-scaling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Effective fields cannot be used for Search nodes. The Terraform database-node effective-fields workflow therefore cannot be treated as a Search-node sizing control. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Issue #1214 reports ASYMMETRIC_HARDWARE_INVALID on provider 1.9.0 when electable and analytics tiers differ, with the error naming the v1.0 API. This historical cross-node-type hardware failure is distinct from present per-shard asymmetry and does not establish a current advanced_cluster limitation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-06-07)

For supported effective-fields configurations, Atlas preserves running instance_size, disk_size_gb and disk_iops when auto-scaling remains enabled before and after an update. A manual change requires temporarily disabling the relevant auto-scaling, applying the desired specifications, then re-enabling it; a new compute range must contain the current effective instance size. These workflows must not be assumed to overcome the documented multi-shard limitation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Do not rely on list-index lifecycle.ignore_changes to preserve Atlas-managed instance_size, disk_size_gb, or disk_iops during changes to multi-shard topology: the provider explicitly warns against this, and Terraform index syntax identifies a list position rather than a stable Atlas shard identity. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The current advanced_cluster resource defines one replication_specs object per shard. Within a zone the configurations must match except for independently scalable instance_size and disk_iops; this does not imply arbitrary per-shard differences in every hardware field. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

For multi-shard updates, the provider correlates replication_specs entries with shards by list position. Keep existing entries ordered, append new shards after existing entries, and leave existing entries unchanged in that update. The resource documentation recommends contacting MongoDB Support before shard removal or other significant production topology changes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Where effective-fields behavior is supported, use_effective_fields retains client-specified electable_specs, read_only_specs and analytics_specs while effective_electable_specs, effective_read_only_specs and effective_analytics_specs in the advanced_cluster data source expose actual hardware. This is a distinction between configured and running specifications, not an instruction to resize Search nodes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Issue #1544 reports noisy whole-block replication_specs diffs with Terraform 1.4.6 and mongodbatlas provider 1.12.0 on the legacy mongodbatlas_cluster resource. Its example still labels the resource update in-place; this historical report is not evidence that the current advanced_cluster resource recreates a cluster for every nested change. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-10-20)
